content: 1. Lopinavir/ritonavir should not be administered as a once-daily dose in children or adolescents. Instead, it should be given every 12 hours. The safety and efficacy of this medication in children under 2 weeks of age have not been established. 2. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases alfuzosin levels through the same mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Amiodarone also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Ritonavir further increases amiodarone levels by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of astemizole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Cobicistat increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases cobimetinib levels through the same mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases conivaptan levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. Conivaptan should not be used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases dihydroergotamine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases intranasal dihydroergotamine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Disulfiram increases the toxicity of ritonavir by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This interaction is only associated with the oral solution of ritonavir, which contains 42% alcohol. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Lopinavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of ALT elevations caused by increased grazoprevir plasma concentrations. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. Elagolix should not be used with strong OATP1B1 inhibitors. 15. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as this combination is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be used with other antiretrovirals. 18. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir, in turn, increases enzalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases ergoloid mesylates levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases ergonovine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases finerenone levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases flibanserin levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 24. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases gepirone levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Goserelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lopinavir also increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of liposomal irinotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lopinavir similarly increases liposomal irinotecan levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases ivabradine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe bradycardia. 30. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 31. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Lopinavir increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases lomitapide levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases lonafarnib levels. Co-administration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 34. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases lovastatin levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 35. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases mavacamten levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure caused by systolic dysfunction. 37. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as mavorixafor is a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases methylergonovine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases naloxegol levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 40. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Ritonavir increases the levels of pimozide by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 42. Lopinavir increases the levels of pitavastatin by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases regorafenib levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Lopinavir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases salmeterol levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of increased toxicity. 45. Lopinavir increases the levels of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir similarly increases simvastatin levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 46. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 47. Lopinavir increases the levels of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of lopinavir by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This interaction is only associated with the oral solution of lopinavir, which contains 42% alcohol. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 51. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir similarly increases venetoclax levels. Co-administration is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. 52. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated.
